land.text: García I's share of 910: León, without Fruela's Asturias but with the eastern marches around Burgos

predecessors.note: 'It was founded in 910, when the Christian princes of Asturias' (Alfonso III's sons forced his abdication in 910 and the kingdom split in three); Cliopatria starts the León row in 911.

land.text: Galicia, ruled by Ordoño from 910 and joined to León on García I's death in 914

predecessors.note: 'When García died in 914, León went to Ordoño, who now ruled both León and Galicia as Ordoño II.' Cliopatria draws the union from 922.

land.text: León, León's Extremadura and Galicia, united with Castile for good

successors.note: 'Permanent union of Castile and León: 10 December 1230' (infobox); the Castile dossier cites 23 September and 11 December 1230 for the same union from other pages. From 1236 Cliopatria's Crown of Castile row (crown-of-castile) carries the whole.

capitals.name: León
capitals.note: 'García I (910–914) who moved the capital of the kingdom of Astures to León' (Oviedo to León). Zamora, Compostela or Toledo hosted courts; the page does not move the seat.

union.text: the eastern lands Cliopatria labels Asturias in 911-925 (Burgos, Cantabria, La Rioja, Soria)

correction.text: León without Asturias, with the eastern marches around Burgos; holds 910-913

keyframe_review.note: 59,553 km2 for 911-921: León, Palencia, Zamora, Valladolid and northern Portugal (Porto to Coimbra), with 21 of Asturias' 41 cells. The Asturias page says Fruela kept Asturias until 924 and Galicia was Ordoño's until 914, so the shape holds from 910 to 913 with Asturias taken out and the eastern lands that Cliopatria labels 'Asturias' (29,428 km2 around Burgos) put in: 'Burgos remained within Leon until the 930s' and 'During the early 10th century, León expanded to the south and east'. The page gives no infobox area.

union.text: the eastern lands Cliopatria labels Asturias in 911-925 (Burgos, Cantabria, La Rioja, Soria)

correction.text: León with Galicia and the eastern marches, without Asturias; holds 914-923

keyframe_review.note: 105,160 km2 for 922-925: the 911 shape plus Galicia (Lugo, Corunna, Orense, Pontevedra, Viana do Castelo). The page puts the union in 914 ('When García died in 914, León went to Ordoño, who now ruled both León and Galicia'), eight years before Cliopatria; Asturias stays out until 924.

correction.text: León with Galicia, Asturias and the eastern marches, all under one crown

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 924-930: Fruela II 'became king with his royal court in León' in 924 and the kingdom of Asturias 'transitioned into the Kingdom of León in 924'. This is the shape Cliopatria draws from 926 (134,237 km2); Cliopatria's Asturias row ends in 925.

minus.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

correction.text: León without the County of Castile; holds 931-939

keyframe_review.note: 134,237 km2 for 926-946 holds the County of Castile (Burgos, Soria, La Rioja, Cantabria, 40,000 km2) inside León. 'The County of Castile split off in 931' (Leon page); the Castile dossier cites its County of Castile page for Fernán González's reunification of the county in 931. Cliopatria separates Castile only in 961. The shape applies to 931-939; the Duero-Tormes belt comes in 939 (next verdict).

minus.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

correction.text: León with the Duero-Tormes belt, without Castile; holds 940-960

keyframe_review.note: 183,504 km2 for 947-960: 49,267 km2 more than 926, the Salamanca-Ávila-Segovia belt and Viseu-Guarda. 'He defeated the hosts of the Umayyad caliph, Abd al-Rahman III, at the Battle of Simancas (939)'; 'This victory allowed the advance of the Leonese border of the Duero to the Tormes.' The page dates no step, so the belt is dated to 939 and the shape applies from 940; the County of Castile (split off in 931) stays out until 960. Cliopatria's Caliphate row loses exactly the same area in 947.

144,145 km2 for 961-989: Castile has left (Cliopatria's Castile row begins in 961). Ramiro III (966-982) is on the throne; a Viking fleet of 100 ships landed in Galicia in 968 and 'In 971, Gunrod and his Vikings were surprised and defeated' (no land moved).

132,745 km2 for 990-1009: the Mondego (Coimbra, Aveiro) and the Beira are lost and the Duero edge pared back. Almanzor looted Zamora in September 981 and 'attacked Portuguese lands, probably Viseu' a month later; 'In 1008, Galicia and the Douro region were attacked' (Leon page). Raids, not annexations on the pages opened; the shape stands, unverified: page budget.
132,843 km2 for 1010-1033: the same shape. Alfonso V promulgated the Fueros de León in 1017; 'Sancho III of Navarre (1004–1035) took over Castile in the 1020s'.

New keyframe, 1034-1037: Cliopatria has no León shape for 1034-1039. Taken as Vermudo III's kingdom, the 1010 shape unchanged, until Ferdinand I 'defeated and killed his suzerain at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037'. The kingdom-of-pamplona dossier (eu-12-a) has Sancho III of Navarre taking León in 1034 with the western lands leaving him in 1035; no page opened for this dossier says so (the Leon page has only that Sancho 'took over Castile in the 1020s'), so this is flagged, not adopted.

correction.text: León under Ferdinand I, king of Castile and León

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1038-1039: Ferdinand I 'on 22 June 1038 had himself crowned and anointed king in León'; the kingdom is his second crown, the same shape as 1040.
133,301 km2 for 1040-1045: León drawn beside Castile (34,277 km2) under one king; 'For nearly 30 years, until his death in 1065, he ruled over the kingdom of León' (Leon page).

69,043 km2 for 1066-1071: Alfonso's share after 'By his will, Ferdinand divided his kingdom among his three sons'; 'the region of Galicia was carved off to create a separate state' (García). The shape has no Galicia, matching the page. León was then 'king of León (1065–1109)' for Alfonso VI (Alfonso VI page).

192,464 km2 for 1126-1138: 'On 10 March 1126, after the death of his mother, he was crowned in León'; 'On 26 May 1135, Alfonso was crowned "Emperor of Spain" in the Cathedral of León.' The shape is Alfonso VII's whole realm except Castile proper (Burgos, Soria and the Basque lands, which Cliopatria draws nowhere in 1126-1138: see castile_1126 in the Castile dossier), and includes the Portuguese lands north of the Tagus that become the County of Portugal in 1139.

correction.text: León under Ferdinand II, apart from Castile

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1157-1168: Cliopatria draws the whole of Alfonso VII's realm as Castile until 1168 and León only from 1169; the division took effect on his death in August 1157. 'The two kingdoms of León and Castile were split in 1157' (Leon page); 'dividing his realm between his sons' with the infobox 'Successor: Sancho III (Castile), Ferdinand II (León)' (Alfonso VII page, which dates the death 21 August 1157).
110,182 km2 for 1169-1187: León, Galicia, Asturias and the Extremaduran strip around Cáceres (30 of 75 cells). The page gives no infobox area.

126,964 km2 for 1188-1201: Cáceres (68 of 75 cells) and Badajoz (19 of 83) are added. Alfonso IX reigns 'from the death of his father Ferdinand II in 1188'. The page has a failed crusade on Cáceres in 1218 ('poor weather doomed it'), which sits oddly with a Leonese Cáceres in 1188; no page opened dates a conquest then. Unverified: page budget; the reviewer may prefer the 1169 shape.

109,600 km2 for 1202-1215: Extremadura pared back to 28 of 75 Cáceres cells and none of Badajoz. 'Treaties made in 1205, 1207, and 1209 each forced him to concede further territories and rights' (to Castile); the shapes show no matching change on the Castilian border. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1202 shape, without the Extremadura increment that the page puts in 1230

keyframe_review.note: 131,304 km2 for 1216-1219: Cáceres (68 of 75) and Badajoz (29 of 83) again. 'In 1218, Alfonso launched a crusade to capture Cáceres, but poor weather doomed it' and 'capturing Mérida and Badajoz in 1230': the increment over 1202 is not supported before 1229-1230, so the 1202 shape holds.

correction.text: the 1202 shape, without the Extremadura increment that the page puts in 1230

keyframe_review.note: 131,422 km2 for 1220-1226: same Extremadura increment as 1216; same correction.

147,015 km2 for 1227-1235 (to the south of 37.8 N, touching Seville, Huelva and Córdoba): Badajoz (77 of 83) and Cáceres are full. The page dates Mérida and Badajoz to 1230, so 1227-1229 is the 1202 shape (next keyframe: 1230); León ends in December 1230, and 1231-1235 is the Castile row's union (castile_1231).

correction.text: the 1202 shape plus Mérida and Badajoz

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1230 only: 'capturing Mérida and Badajoz in 1230, which allowed for the eventual conquest of Seville'. The last year of the kingdom: Alfonso IX died 24 September 1230 and the union with Castile followed in December.

union.text: the eastern lands Cliopatria labels Asturias in 911-925 (Burgos, Cantabria, La Rioja, Soria)

region.text: León and the eastern marches

ledger.note: 910: García I makes León a kingdom. 'It was founded in 910, when the Christian princes of Asturias' ...; 'García I (910–914) who moved the capital of the kingdom of Astures to León'; the Asturias page: 'When Alfonso III's sons forced his abdication in 910, the Kingdom of Asturias split into three separate kingdoms.' The page names no boundary; the region is the Duero lands of Cliopatria's 911 shape, with the eastern marches.

region.text: Galicia

ledger.note: 914: Ordoño II unites León and Galicia. 'When García died in 914, León went to Ordoño, who now ruled both León and Galicia as Ordoño II.' (The Asturias page: 'León and Galicia in 914, Asturias later'.) Cliopatria draws the union from 922.

region.text: Asturias joins León

ledger.note: 924: Asturias joins León. 'The Kingdom of Asturias transitioned into the Kingdom of León in 924 when Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León'; infobox 'Annexed by the Kingdom of León: 924'.

region.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

ledger.note: 931: the County of Castile splits off. 'The County of Castile split off in 931' (Leon page); The Ramiro II page adds that Fernán González gained 'brief de facto independence' late in Ramiro's reign. The land is Cliopatria's later Castile shape.

region.text: the belt between the Duero and the Tormes

ledger.note: 937: the caliph's campaign in León. 'In 937 Abd al-Rahman conquered some thirty castles in León'; the Battle of Simancas follows in 939 and a peace in 951.

region.text: the belt between the Duero and the Tormes

ledger.note: 939: Simancas moves the frontier to the Tormes. 'He defeated the hosts of the Umayyad caliph, Abd al-Rahman III, at the Battle of Simancas (939)'; 'This victory allowed the advance of the Leonese border of the Duero to the Tormes.' The page gives no year for the advance; Cliopatria draws it from 947.

region.text: the belt between the Duero and the Tormes

ledger.note: 951: peace with the caliph. 'In 951 he signed a peace with the new king of León.' Ramiro II had died on 1 January 951 and 'Still in 950 Ramiro launched an expedition to the valley of the Edge and defeated the Cordovan Umayyads at Talavera' (Ramiro II page).

region.text: the Mondego, the Beira and the Duero edge that León held in 989 and not in 990

ledger.note: 990: the Mondego and the Beira fall away. Cliopatria's shape loses Coimbra, Aveiro and part of Viseu, Guarda and Segovia in 990; the Almanzor page has raids only (Zamora looted in September 981, 'Portuguese lands, probably Viseu'), so the date is a bridge over a silence.

region.text: León, drawn inside the Castile row 1046-1065

ledger.note: 1046: Ferdinand I's two kingdoms are drawn as one. Cliopatria stops drawing León apart in 1046 and shows Ferdinand's whole realm as one Castile shape until 1065; the pages date only Tamarón (4 September 1037) and the coronation in León (22 June 1038). León stays a kingdom: 'he ruled over the kingdom of León' to 1065.

region.text: León, Alfonso VI's share

ledger.note: 1065: Ferdinand I's kingdom is divided and León goes to Alfonso. 'By his will, Ferdinand divided his kingdom among his three sons'; 'Ferdinand died on 24 December 1065, in León'; Alfonso VI is 'king of León (1065–1109)'.

region.text: León, absorbed first by Sancho II and then by Alfonso VI's reunited realm

ledger.note: 1072: Sancho II defeats Alfonso at Golpejera. 'The truce was broken with the Battle of Golpejera on 12 January 1072'; Sancho invaded Galicia in 1071 and was murdered during the siege of Zamora, after which Alfonso VI took back León, Castile and Galicia ('and Castile (1072–1109)'). Cliopatria draws the reunited realm as the Castile row 1072-1110.

region.text: León, Galicia, the Extremadura and the Toledo country

ledger.note: 1126: Alfonso VII is crowned in León. 'On 10 March 1126, after the death of his mother, he was crowned in León.' Cliopatria draws León again as its own row 1126-1138 (it had been inside the Castile row since 1072). The Peace of Támara (1127) recognised him against the king of Aragon.

region.text: the lands of Cliopatria's León 1126 that are not in the Castile 1139 shape: the Portuguese north and Beira

ledger.note: 1139: the Portuguese lands separate. Cliopatria shows a County of Portugal (46,123 km2) from 1139 and drops the Beira from the León/Castile shape; the page gives only 'was recognized as independent de jure in 1143' and 'the Treaty of Zamora (1143)'. The 1139 date is Cliopatria's.

region.text: León, inside Alfonso VII's realm drawn as Castile

ledger.note: 1139: León is drawn inside the Castile row again. Alfonso VII's realm appears as Cliopatria's Castile shape 1139-1168; the pages opened date no change in 1139 ('Emperor of Spain' in 1135, the division in 1157).

region.text: León under Ferdinand II

ledger.note: 1157: Alfonso VII's death splits Castile and León. 'The two kingdoms of León and Castile were split in 1157' (Leon page); Alfonso VII died 21 August 1157 'by dividing his realm between his sons' (Ferdinand II got León). Cliopatria draws León again from 1169.

region.text: Cáceres and Badajoz cells of the 1188 shape

ledger.note: 1188: Extremadura is added to León's shape. Alfonso IX succeeded 'in 1188'; Cliopatria adds Cáceres and Badajoz that year. No page opened dates a conquest then, and the failed 1218 crusade on Cáceres suggests the shape is early.

region.text: the Cáceres and Badajoz cells León held in 1201 and not in 1202

ledger.note: 1202: the Extremaduran increment is gone. Cliopatria's 1202 shape returns to the 1169 outline (Cáceres 28 of 75, Badajoz none); the pages opened do not say why (Alarcos, 1195, and Almohad pressure are the usual reading but are not on the pages opened).

region.text: Mérida and Badajoz

ledger.note: 1230: Alfonso IX takes Mérida and Badajoz. 'capturing Mérida and Badajoz in 1230, which allowed for the eventual conquest of Seville.' The page names no holder and no overlord, so the counterpart is my reading: the Almohad Caliphate, the nearest Muslim power in Cliopatria (its row runs 1139-1343); the page names no holder.

region.text: León

ledger.note: 1230: León is permanently united with Castile. Infobox 'Permanent union of Castile and León: 10 December 1230'; Alfonso IX had died on 24 September 1230 and 'This coronation united the Kingdoms of León and Castile'.

region.text: all of León

ledger.note: 1230: the Kingdom of León ends in the union. Its crown, its Extremadura and Galicia pass to Ferdinand III's realm, which Cliopatria draws as the Castile row to 1235 and the Crown of Castile from 1236.

wars.name: Leonese wars of Abd al-Rahman III (Simancas)

zones.text: the belt between the Duero and the Tormes

wars.outcome: Caliph's army crushed at Simancas in 939; the Leonese border moves from the Duero to the Tormes; peace in 951.
wars.note: Ramiro II (931-951) 'lost the support of García Sánchez I of Pamplona, who helped ... the count Fernán González of Castile, to gain brief de facto independence'; 950: Talavera. The 937 date of the caliph's 'thirty castles' is on the Abd al-Rahman III page.

wars.name: Almanzor's campaigns against León
wars.outcome: Raids on Salamanca, Cuéllar, Zamora (September 981) and 'Portuguese lands, probably Viseu'; no land is shown taken on the page; the 988 sack of León and the 997 sack of Santiago are not on a page read here.
wars.note: Atienza, spring 980, the Castile and Pamplona allies of Ghalib defeated at Torrevicente on 10 July 981; Almanzor died 8 August 1002 at Medinaceli.

wars.name: Battle of Tamarón and Ferdinand I's conquest of León
wars.outcome: Ferdinand I, count of Castile, 'defeated and killed his suzerain at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037' and was crowned king in León on 22 June 1038: Castile and León under one king, still two kingdoms.
wars.note: No border moves in Cliopatria; León is drawn separately 1040-1045 and inside the Castile row 1046-1065.

wars.name: War of the sons of Ferdinand I (Sancho II against Alfonso VI and García)

zones.text: León, taken by Sancho II in January 1072

wars.outcome: Sancho II invaded Galicia in 1071, defeated Alfonso VI at Golpejera on 12 January 1072 and was murdered at the siege of Zamora; Alfonso VI took back León and took Castile and Galicia.
wars.note: 'The conflicts began after the death of their mother Queen Sancha on 7 November 1067.' García was imprisoned in 1073 (held 17 years at Luna). The battle of Llantada is not dated on the page.

wars.name: Alfonso IX's wars with Castile (treaties of 1205, 1207 and 1209)
wars.outcome: 'treaties made in 1205, 1207, and 1209 each forced him to concede further territories and rights'; 'In July 1188 his cousin Alfonso VIII of Castile required the younger Alfonso to recognize the elder as overlord'. No change shows in Cliopatria's shapes.

wars.name: Alfonso IX's Extremadura campaigns (Cáceres 1218, Mérida and Badajoz 1230)
wars.outcome: The 1218 crusade on Cáceres failed ('poor weather doomed it'); Mérida and Badajoz were captured in 1230.
wars.note: In 1211 Alfonso IX 'gave the castle of Alcañices to the Templar Order'.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the caliphate, the taifas, Castile and Navarre are marches; the pages opened give no surveyed line. The Leon-Castile line is a treaty line only in 1205-1209 (no coordinates) and the partition of 1157 (no line).

sources.title: Kingdom of León
sources.note: Identity: founded 910, García I moves the capital to León, Galicia 914, Castile split off 931, Ferdinand I 1037, 1157 split, 1230 union (10 December). No infobox area.

sources.title: Ramiro II of León
sources.note: Simancas 939 and the advance of the border from the Duero to the Tormes (undated), Talavera 950, death 1 January 951.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman III
sources.note: The caliph's side of the 937-951 wars: thirty castles 937, Simancas 939, peace 951; homage of 958; Zamora 959 and Oviedo 960.

sources.title: Almanzor
sources.note: Raids 977-981 on Salamanca, Zamora and Viseu; death 1002. The fetch covered the article to about 990 only.

sources.title: Kingdom of Asturias
sources.note: The 910 split into three kingdoms, León and Galicia reunited 914, Asturias annexed 924.

sources.title: Ferdinand I of León
sources.note: Tamarón 4 September 1037, crowned in León 22 June 1038, Lamego 1057, Viseu 1058, Coimbra 1064, the division of 1065, death 24 December 1065.

sources.title: Alfonso VI of León and Castile
sources.note: King of León 1065, Golpejera 12 January 1072, Galicia 1071-1073, union 1072, Toledo 1085, Sagrajas 1086, Uclés 1108.

sources.title: Alfonso VII of León and Castile
sources.note: Crowned in León 10 March 1126, Emperor 26 May 1135, Portugal independent 1143, Coria 1142, Almería 1147, death 21 August 1157 and the division.

sources.title: Alfonso IX of León
sources.note: Accession 1188, treaties 1205/1207/1209, Cáceres crusade 1218, Mérida and Badajoz 1230, death 24 September 1230.

notes: Cliopatria rows and what is not settled. (1) The Kingdom of Castile and León alternate in Cliopatria: León is drawn separately 911-1045 (gap 1034-1039 filled with new keyframes), 1066-1071, 1126-1138 and 1169-1235; the union under one king is drawn as the Castile row 1046-1065, 1072-1125 and 1139-1168. The Leon dossier keeps that allocation and records the passes as loss/gain events with kingdom-of-castile as counterpart (1046 conf 1, 1065, 1072, 1126, 1139 conf 1, 1157); the Castile dossier carries the mirror events. (2) 1126-1138: the Leon row holds all of Alfonso VII's realm except Castile proper, which Cliopatria draws nowhere; the Castile dossier adds castile_1126. (3) The County of Castile is inside the Leon shapes until 960 in Cliopatria; the pages say it split off in 931, so the 926 and 947 shapes are cut by the Castile 961 shape from 931. (4) The Cliopatria 'Kingdom of Asturias' row (911-925, 29,428 km2 around Burgos) is treated as Leonese land (the Leon page: Burgos stayed in León until the 930s); the kingdom-of-asturias dossier (eu-12-a) marks it wrong and says the holder is undated, so the two dossiers agree that it is not Asturias. (5) The Leon page for the Galicia year: 914 on the Leon page and the Asturias page; Cliopatria 922. The kingdom-of-galicia dossier (not yet written when this was done) draws Galicia separately to 921 and will overlap this one for 914-921. (6) Extremadura 1188-1230: Cliopatria's Cáceres/Badajoz increments in the 1188 and 1216-1227 shapes conflict with the Alfonso IX page (failed Cáceres crusade 1218, Mérida and Badajoz 1230); 1216-1227 corrected to the 1202 shape, 1188 left unverified. (7) End of the kingdom: the Leon page gives 10 December 1230; the Castile dossier cites 23 September 1230 (Kingdom of Castile page) and the treaty of Benavente on 11 December 1230 (Ferdinand III page); Cliopatria draws both kingdoms to 1235. (8) Rulers omitted: the fetch of the Leon page returned only some reigns (García I 910-914, Ordoño II 914-924, Ramiro II 931-951, Ramiro III 966-982, Ferdinand I 1038-1065, Alfonso VI 1065-1109, Alfonso VII 1126-1157, Alfonso IX 1188-1230); a gap-filler should open the page's list. (9) Not on a page read: the sack of León (988) and Santiago (997) by Almanzor, the loss of the Beira (Coimbra 987), Ferdinand II's Extremadura (1157-1188), Urraca's reign (1109-1126) and the division of Alfonso VII in detail. (10) Gazetteer: Tormes has no entry (the Duero-Tormes belt is Cliopatria's 947 minus 926 shape). Page budget: nine pages (one fewer than the Castile dossier needs for Ferdinand III).
